findings.scenario: You read this spec to decide whether the gate is worth building. It opens by naming two bugs that already shipped and says this gate stops that class. You approve it, it gets built, and you believe both holes are now covered. Only one of them is. The second bug was caused by a build cache on the hosting side serving a stale answer -- and a container that builds from scratch has no cache to serve, so it cannot reproduce that failure at all. Worse, the two guards that DO hold that bug shut go unnamed in this spec, so the next person tidying up sees a shiny new gate and prunes them.
findings.whats_wrong: The doc presents NH-315 as a bug this gate would catch. The changelog records its mechanism as a branch-keyed Vercel build cache that outlived a change to what Tailwind scans. A cold container build cannot reproduce that. Of the two cited incidents the gate catches PR #162's 0-px seek rail, not NH-315.
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by primary sources: decision-changelog.md:483 names the branch-keyed cache mechanism ('outlived a change to what Tailwind scans'). Both remedies exist and AGENTS.md:111 says they must stay -- web/vercel.json:5 removes .next/cache, and REQUIRED_SELECTORS lives at web/scripts/assert-design-system-css.mjs:62, run by web's own build script.
findings.fix: In 'Why this exists', state NH-315's real mechanism, that a cold container build cannot reproduce it, and that it is already held shut by web/vercel.json's .next/cache removal plus the assert-design-system-css.mjs REQUIRED_SELECTORS canary -- so of the two cited incidents this gate would have caught the PR #162 rail, not NH-315. Add a fourth 'Approaches weighed' row for that canary, verdict 'complement, not substitute'. Restate the Storybook rejection's third count as the coverage this gate actually adds (the composed page's pixels at a real width) instead of 'never runs next build'.
findings.knock_on: MUST ALSO EDIT line 34, 'The bug class has already shipped twice:'. Reclassifying NH-315 without rewriting that lead-in makes the section contradict itself.

findings.whats_wrong: The guard's pattern requires skip or fixme immediately after `test.`, so it matches test.skip( but not test.describe.skip( -- and this design already needs a test.describe() wrapper for the narrow-viewport shot, which makes skipping the describe the natural way to park it.
findings.verified: PARTIAL. The miss is real and measured. But the reviewer's proposed replacement is half wrong on BOTH counts: dropping the trailing \( makes it match any TEXT occurrence ('test.skip.png' in a snapshot name, '// never use test.skip here', 'const skip = test.skip;'), and its stated reason -- 'so no-argument call forms are caught' -- is FALSE: test.skip() and test.fixme() are calls the CURRENT pattern already matches.
findings.fix: CORRECTED BY VERIFICATION -- apply this, not the reviewer's original. Use /\btest\.(?:describe\.)?(?:skip|fixme)\s*\(/ . Measured truth table: catches test.skip(, test.fixme(, test.describe.skip(, test.describe.fixme( and test.skip ( cond ); rejects test.describe(, test.describe.configure(, test.step(, test.slow(, skipIf( and every string/comment case. DROP the no-argument rationale from the doc -- it is false.

findings.fix: Add a second assertion to the same tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs test: read web/playwright.e2e.config.ts and require both `name: 'chromium'` and `testMatch: '**/*.vr.ts'`, so deleting or renaming the project fails the guard instead of silently emptying the lane.

findings.verdict: PARTIAL -- finding real, reviewer's fix WRONG REMEDY
findings.scenario: Screenshots start flaking. You reach for the one-line escape hatch the spec promises and find it barely helps, because it only serialises the shots against each other -- 91 behaviour tests keep hammering the same server in parallel, which is where the contention actually comes from. You are now debugging a flaky merge gate with the remedy the document told you would fix it.
findings.whats_wrong: `fullyParallel: false` on the VR project serialises only tests WITHIN each file; test files still run in parallel, so the behaviour tests keep running concurrently against the same server. It does not restore the conditions the 60-run stability study was measured under.
findings.verified: PARTIAL. The defect is CONFIRMED and measured: Playwright's own types plus a timestamped run show project-level fullyParallel:false serialised the two shots 57 ms apart while both behaviour files ran concurrently with them. web/playwright.e2e.config.ts:9 sets fullyParallel: true config-wide. BUT the reviewer's premise that `workers` is config-level only is WRONG -- TestProject.workers exists. And its proposed remedy (replace the hatch with a separate web-vr job) is the wrong first move: the doc's own table prices that at a third web build, and the doc ALREADY names that fallback two lines below the hatch at :711.
findings.fix: CORRECTED BY VERIFICATION -- apply this, not the reviewer's original. Do NOT delete the one-line hatch. Instead: (a) add the caveat that fullyParallel:false serialises only the shots inside each file and leaves the behaviour tests concurrent against the same server; (b) record Playwright's first-class remedy, `dependencies: ['e2e']` on the chromium project, which MEASURED under one unscoped invocation: both behaviour files finish, THEN the shots run -- pair it with fullyParallel:false or workers:1 to serialise the shots among themselves; (c) keep the separate web-vr job as the documented fallback, not the first remedy.
fix_cautions: RECORD THE MEASURED TRADE-OFF of dependencies: one failing behaviour test makes the dependent project report '2 did not run'. The run is red so merge still blocks, but it compares ZERO pixels -- and retries: 2 means a persistent failure costs the whole pixel lane.

Verified NOT a contradiction of settled 9 (one unscoped invocation) or settled 10 (parallel shots): the doc already names the web-vr fallback at :711 alongside settled 9, and dependencies works under a single unscoped invocation.
This is the same inverted-fix shape lap 4 hit with its own L4-F-7. Present the CORRECTED fix; do not offer the reviewer's 'replace the hatch' version.

fyi_observations.scenario: You copy the assertion snippet the spec gives you into a new shot file and the build fails on a type error before a single screenshot is taken.
fyi_observations.whats_wrong: web/tsconfig.json is strict and includes **/*.ts, so web/e2e/*.vr.ts is typechecked, and el.parentElement is HTMLElement | null where getComputedStyle takes Element. The logic is sound -- the panel's parent is in practice a non-null wrapper -- only the nil path is unhandled.
fyi_observations.verified: CONFIRMED by running tsc. web/tsconfig.json:7 is strict and includes **/*.ts. The snippet verbatim gives `error TS2345: Argument of type 'HTMLElement | null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Element'` (exit 2). The guarded rewrite compiles clean (exit 0).
fyi_observations.fix: Hoist and guard the parent: `const parent = el.parentElement;` then `return parent !== null && own !== getComputedStyle(parent).backgroundColor && own !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)';`
fyi_observations.route: FYI -- anchor 50. Reported, NOT a decision. Does not consume the triage cap. NOTE: it is a real typecheck failure against a CI gate, so the maintainer may well want it applied despite the FYI routing -- worth one line at the end of triage.
